title: ChroDrip - ProteinA
author: David Frommholz
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.uweexbe
materials: Do you want to purify antibodies or sanitize your column? Please choose below.

steps.title: Load sample onto column
steps.instruction: Add the sample to the top of the column and let it flow through by gravity. Adjust the sample to pH 7.5‑8.5 and 150‑300 mM NaCl; a convenient way is to add 1/11 volume of 0.5 M Tris, 2 M NaCl (pH 8.0). Remove particulate matter by centrifugation or 0.45 µm filtration. For slow or weak‑binding antibodies, collect the flow‑through and re‑apply it.

steps.title: Wash column with buffer
steps.instruction: Add 5 column volumes (CV) of wash buffer and wait until it has drained. Repeat once more. Keep the flow‑through and wash fractions for later analysis (e.g., SDS‑PAGE). For higher purity, repeat the washing step up to a total of 5 times. If needed, supplement the wash buffer with up to 1 % Tween‑20 and/or up to 0.5 M NaCl.

steps.title: Pre‑elution buffer addition
steps.instruction: Add 0.75 CV of elution buffer to the column. This pre‑elution step does not contain the target protein but replaces most of the wash buffer, yielding a more concentrated eluate.

steps.title: Elute target protein
steps.instruction: Place a clean tube under the column. Add three successive aliquots of 3 CV elution buffer (total 9 CV), collecting each fraction in a separate tube and waiting for complete drainage between aliquots. For more concentrated eluates, instead perform eight successive elutions of 1 CV each, collecting each fraction separately. Determine which fractions contain most protein and combine them.

steps.title: Prepare column for cleaning
steps.instruction: Remove the bottom and top caps of the column. If the column has been used, first drain the storage solution. Then add 5 CV of wash buffer (use the bed volume indicated on the column).

steps.title: Sequential wash and storage preparation
steps.instruction: Wash the column successively with 5 CV elution buffer, 5 CV wash buffer, and 5 CV deionized water. Next, add 10 CV of 20 % ethanol or wash buffer containing 0.05 % (w/v) sodium azide and wait until half of the buffer has drained. Close the top lid and then the bottom stopper. Store the column at room temperature or at 4‑8 °C. For long‑term storage, dry the open column (top and bottom) in an oven at 80 °C for at least 2 hours or overnight, ensuring the bottom stopper is completely dry, then re‑attach the outlet, close the lid, and store the closed column at room temperature.

steps.title: Neutralize eluate
steps.instruction: Add neutralization solution to the eluate at a ratio of three drops per milliliter of eluate.

steps.title: Post‑purification column wash
steps.instruction: After a purification, wash the column with 5 CV elution buffer followed by 5 CV wash buffer and let the buffer drain. If the column had been stored, let it drain and then wash with an additional 5 CV wash buffer.

steps.title: Sanitize column
steps.instruction: Add 5 CV sanitization solution, let 1 CV drain, then close the column with the top and bottom caps. Incubate for 1 hour at room temperature.

steps.title: Drain and final water wash
steps.instruction: Drain the sanitization solution and wash the column with 10 CV deionized water.

steps.title: Final storage wash and drying
steps.instruction: Add approximately 5 CV wash buffer (containing 0.05 % sodium azide) and wait until half of the buffer has drained. Close the top lid and then the bottom stopper. Store the column at room temperature or at 4‑8 °C and wait at least 12 hours before the next purification. For long‑term storage, dry the open column (top and bottom) in an oven at 80 °C for at least 2 hours or overnight, ensure the bottom stopper is dry, re‑attach the outlet, close the lid, and store the closed column at room temperature.
